resumen: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell held with both hands travels behind the head with the arms almost straight and comes back over the chest. Although it is classed as a pull, the chest works at least as much as the lats.
ejecucion: Lie on a bench with your head supported and cup the top end of a dumbbell with both hands, over your chest.
With your elbows slightly bent and fixed, lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head.
Go down until you feel a stretch in your chest and sides, without arching your lower back.
Come back along the same arc until the dumbbell is over your chest again.
matices: It is often taught as a back exercise, but the study that measured it, with a barbell and in eight people, found more pectoralis major than latissimus dorsi activity, and a 2026 narrative review reaches the same reading. Which one works more depends on the range and on where the load sits at each point.
